thread:
incidents-bot: PAGER — euc2: sudden 5xx spike across ingress in eu-central region. alert: ALB/NLB/ingress-controller. page sent to rotation (emma).

emma: i'm on it. seeing 5xx rate from ingress pods in euc2b and euc2c, also a notable increase in `connreset` on NLB metrics.

raj: tagging in netops — any recent infra changes in euc2?

marta: nothing deployed from infra side in the last hour. noticed a DNS flapping alert earlier for euc2 private zone but it auto-recovered. link: https://dash.internal/redwood/dns/euc2?from=now-1h

robin: i'm pulling envoy access logs and ALB target health. grabbing recent `tcp_reset`/`502` samples.

netops-bot: Automated note: Euc2 AZ euc2b reported elevated packet drops on hypervisor level 02:30 UTC. Network team investigating. Incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood/1834005678

emma: ok, two parallel hypotheses: 1) upstream NLB/ALB issue dropping connections -> envoy upstream resets 2) DNS-to-ingress routing intermittently sending traffic to drained targets.

support-lead: customer impact initial: several EU customers report timeouts and errors for prompt generation. estimated affected requests ~8-12% in last 30m; some 5xx errors surfaced in hosted api for eu endpoints.

raj: can we confirm target health states?

robin: `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:...euc2  | jq '.TargetHealthDescriptions[] | {Target: .Target.Id, State: .TargetHealth.State, Reason: .TargetHealth.Reason}'`

robin: result shows ~18% of targets in target-group-euc2-internal are `unhealthy` with reason `Connection timed out` and `Target.ResponseCode: 502`.

emma: checking ingress controller (k8s) — `kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=ingress-controller -o wide` shows some restarts in euc2c.

marta: looking at DNS: private zone record for internal-api.euc2.redwood.local had updates 00:46 UTC from automated failover script, TTL is short (30s). might explain rapid flips.

robin: envoy logs show upstream reset reason `Eof` and `Connection reset by peer`, stack traces pointing at early TLS handshake failure for some connections. snippet:

```
[2026-03-15T00:48:12Z] envoy upstream reset: reason=CONNECTION_FAILURE, details=error during SSL handshake, peer closed connection
[2026-03-15T00:48:13Z] cluster: internal-backend-euc2 target ip=10.2.5.34 reset
```

emma: so combined symptoms: NLB/ALB target health unstable, envoy upstream TLS/conn resets, DNS flaps causing routing churn. mitigation plan: 1) pause automated DNS failover (marta) 2) mark suspect targets out of rotation and drain gracefully 3) scale up healthy ingress pods to absorb load 4) fail open to other regions for non-PII routes if possible.

marta: pausing automated failover now — `runbook dns > pause-auto-failover` executed. will monitor for stabilization.

raj: netops, can we check if there were hypervisor maintenance events?

netops-bot: Querying cloud telemetry... found maintenance window for host pool euc2b at 00:30 UTC, live-migration events observed correlated with packet drop window. Ticket: CLD-4521.

robin: initiating graceful drain on affected targets: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=10.2.5.34 Id=10.2.5.36` and placing them in cordon state in k8s.

emma: scaling ingress: `kubectl -n infra scale deploy ingress-controller --replicas=8` (was 3). will spin up extra nodes in euc2 and euc1 as hot standby.

support-lead: note to support: set expectations: we see intermittent 5xxs in EU, mitigation in progress, advise fallback to other regions for critical workloads.

marta: DNS pause completed. TTL still low but changes should stop propagating.

emma: after drain + scale, 5xx rate dropped from 11% -> 3% in 6 min. latency p95 improved by ~200ms. chart: https://dash.internal/redwood/alerts/1834005678/charts

robin: confirmed NLB `active_reset_count` trending down after we removed unhealthy targets.

raj: cross-region routing: should we enable automatic routing fallback to eu-west? pros: reduces error surface; cons: e2e latency increase and potential data residency issues. support-lead: get CX approval if we route EU traffic out-of-region.

support-lead: I've pinged the affected customers with a brief notice and offered a targeted mitigation plan for those on dedicated capacity.

emma: next actions: 1) keep DNS paused for 30m 2) monitor target health and envoy resets 3) prepare rollback of DNS pause in case of no improvements 4) file post-incident with timeline and customer impact.

netops-bot: scheduled check-in in 15m.

robin: leaving detailed logs + commands in the incident tracker. snippet of commands used for recovery:

```
# mark targets out
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn $TG --targets Id=$IP1 Id=$IP2
# cordon nodes
kubectl cordon node/euc2-node-12
# scale
kubectl -n infra scale deploy ingress-controller --replicas=8
```

marta: I'm handing off to night oncall (robin) at 01:15 UTC. leaving runbook notes: `dns pause`, `targets drained`, `scale to 8`, `monitor envoy reset rate`.

robin: oncall ack. i'll watch metrics and coordinate with netops for host pool follow-up.

support-lead: updated customers. tracking impacted tenants and will escalate if SLA thresholds breached.

incidents-bot: Update: active alerts reduced. Please update incident status when stable.

emma: marking incident as mitigated for now. will leave as P1 until traffic fully normalizes and postmortem is created.

robin: filing postmortem stub now and assigning to marta (dns), netops (host pool), and infra (ingress scaling).

marta: noted. adding timeline and DNS diffs in PM.

support-lead: thanks team — great fast coordination. :thumbsup:
